Gene Description

DLG4 encodes PSD-95, a membrane-associated guanylate kinase family scaffold concentrated in the intracellular postsynaptic density of excitatory synapses. Its PDZ domains recognize receptor and accessory-protein tails, while its SH3–GK region recruits signaling and scaffold partners, including phosphorylation-dependent ligands. Together these contacts organize neurotransmitter receptors and downstream signaling machinery, support receptor targeting and maintain postsynaptic architecture. The GK-like domain functions in recognition rather than guanylate kinase catalysis. PSD-95 also occupies trafficking, presynaptic and non-neuronal junctional pools in particular contexts. Alternative N termini provide distinct targeting mechanisms, including the palmitoylation-associated alpha and L27-containing beta forms.

Summary: Resolve broad cytoplasmic localization into supported intracellular pools.
Reason: The imported orthology/rule assignment is biologically sound. GO:0035865 cellular response to potassium ion
IEA
GO_REF:0000107 		MARK AS OVER ANNOTATED
Summary: The cited potassium-stimulation result measures regulation of PSD-95 abundance.
Reason: Original PMID:26609151 shows PSD-95 loss after high-KCl stimulation, blocked by proteasome inhibition. The significant additional MAP1A-dependent effect concerns PSD-93, not PSD-95. The process assignment therefore exceeds the specific assay, while the measured change remains valid. This is not a universal rejection of response-term inference from regulated abundance.

Core Functions

PSD-95 bridges synaptic receptors and downstream signaling/scaffold proteins through PDZ-mediated receptor recognition and SH3–GK partner recruitment. These contacts organize receptor targeting and signaling at excitatory postsynaptic sites.

Molecular Function:
synaptic receptor adaptor activity
Directly Involved In:
neurotransmitter receptor localization to postsynaptic specialization membrane
Cellular Locations:
postsynaptic density, intracellular component
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:22117215
    The bindings of PSD-95 SH3-GK to DLGAP1 and SPAR are also phosphorylation-dependent
  • PMID:17046693
    PSD-95 and PSD-93 independently mediate AMPA-R targeting at mature synapses.

PSD-95 provides structural elements of the intracellular postsynaptic density that maintain its protein organization and stabilize receptor-associated scaffold assemblies. This architectural role cooperates with its receptor-adaptor activity.

Molecular Function:
structural constituent of postsynaptic density
Directly Involved In:
maintenance of postsynaptic density structure
Cellular Locations:
postsynaptic density, intracellular component
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:21525273

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Which zero-composite or identity-unresolved PDZ fragment pairs can be confirmed with the exact native partner sequence and an independently controlled full-length assay?

Q: What trafficking and interaction properties distinguish the natural 721-residue product from PSD95-alpha and PSD95-beta?

Q: What target-resolved evidence supports the specific endoplasmic-reticulum, synaptic-vesicle, mossy-fiber-rosette and epithelial-polarity assertions that remain uncertain?

📚 Additional Documentation

Notes

(DLG4-notes.md)

DLG4 review notes

2026-10-17 — source-based review

The review preserves all 575 deterministic source annotations from 577 raw GOA records. Three raw records have identical seeded source fields and form one annotation; assignment/date identifiers remain in the source reconciliation. All three official product identities are retained. Normal UniProt, GOA, publication, GO-CAM and provider outputs remain machine-source records.

The biological synthesis is one synaptic receptor adaptor function: receptor recognition, SH3–GK recruitment and postsynaptic structural support cooperate in receptor organization. The source guide records primary-source locators, product/construct distinctions, pathway paths and actual access limits. The public measurement artifact makes every original fragmentomics value and sequence selection reproducible.

Positive binding interfaces are retained without assuming native full-length interactions or deriving physiological peptide-binding function from short assay reagents. Independent APBA1 co-complex and DLGAP4 GK evidence are explicitly separated from their zero-composite PDZ assays. Repeated partners were checked across sources; differences in the targeted phosphorylation assays and the disputed ERBB4 report preserve their particular evidence scopes.

The final calcium-sign refinement follows the original Figure 3 and shRNA Results of PMID:20531396(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2927054/): its inhibitory 5-HT2A context does not imply a global calcium effect. The original positive annotation remains unchanged as imported metadata. Positive mouse epithelial junctional localization is retained separately from unresolved DLG4 polarity. The KCl experiments establish regulated degradation, while their process assignment remains over-extended for the specific assay.

PMID:16767099(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16767099/) is flagged DISPUTED because of the verified expression of concern, not marked retracted. This does not negate independent ERBB4 association studies.

The default research-provider attempts failed with authentication/quota responses; no provider report was fabricated. Manual primary-source research and the independent core consultation supply the synthesis. Normal caches retain their actual access flags, including abstracts for papers whose originals were separately recovered or partly indexed. No completion credit is implied by this review record.

The shared PMID:10725395 publication file is an explicit exception to the initial cache set: its genuine full-text DLG3 cache was adopted unchanged after identity and byte reconciliation. The original abstract-only fetch remains preserved in provenance. No flag or publication text was manually edited.

2026-10-17 — binding limits and complementary postsynaptic roles

PSD-95 combines receptor-adaptor contacts with a physical contribution to postsynaptic-density architecture. Human SH3–GK fragment experiments demonstrate phosphorylation-sensitive partner recognition; rat-neuron immunogold and tomography place PSD-95 in vertical structural elements, and depletion removes patches of PSD material. The two structured core entries describe cooperating molecular roles, not separate proteins or independent catalytic pathways. Rat tomographic receptor assignments are putative, and the structural observations are not claimed as direct human ultrastructure measurements (PMID:22117215(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243629/); PMID:21525273(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21525273/)). This explicit structural entry supersedes the earlier single-entry representation above. AMPA clustering, NMDA-associated signaling and plasticity retain their evidence-specific annotations as consequences of receptor organization and scaffold function; one core per downstream phenotype is unnecessary.

The fragmentomics zero composites require assay-specific interpretation. All three matched PDZ measurements for each of the 138 undecided zero-only pairs use DAPF, with normalized binding intensity below 0.05 and no independently positive matched fluorescence-polarization result. These are unquantified interactions under the tested conditions, not measured zero affinity or biological nonbinding. Negative intensities describe depletion relative to the control/noise. The original study uses different thresholds for other holdup formats and explicitly cautions against a noninteraction inference below threshold; isolated fragments also do not establish a native full-length complex (PMID:36115835(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9482650/)).

The calcium-sign refinement remains specific to the 5-HT2A neuronal assay: receptor antagonist, terminal-mutant peptide and scrambled-shRNA controls support an inhibitory PSD-95 context, without a global calcium-regulation claim (PMID:20531396(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2927054/), Figure 3). High-KCl experiments instead measure regulated PSD-95 degradation; the significant extra MAP1A effect is on PSD-93. The observed abundance change is retained without claiming that the degraded PSD-95 performs the potassium-response step (PMID:26609151(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26609151/), Results/Figure 7).

The current official GO:0099562 definition says presynaptic despite its postsynaptic label and the explicit part_of edge from structural constituent of postsynaptic density. This ontology-text discrepancy is recorded, not converted into a presynaptic functional assertion. All original annotations, products and machine caches remain unchanged.

Bioinformatics Results

(RESULTS.md)

DLG4 fragmentomics: source values and interpretation

The human DLG4 review contains 388 source assertions from PMID:36115835(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36115835/). This analysis reads the published SD1 workbook, 41467_2022_33018_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx, from the Europe PMC supplement archive. The workbook SHA-256 is ada912921164f0a79630c6a714b9ff264a7217ad3e646153ef498eb456206795.

What the tables contain

There are 1,344 original DLG4 domain measurements: 448 each for PDZ1, PDZ2 and PDZ3. Matching the review's partner accessions creates 1,197 candidate crosswalk rows. Of these, 1,179 match a natural sequence exactly; 18 do not match the natural-sequence field. Three of the latter are AXIN1 internal ligands whose explicitly capped peptide core matches the saved protein sequence. Thus 1,182 measurements are selected by sequence support. Candidate mapping is not equivalent to exact matching, positive binding or a native interaction.

The selected measurements give nonzero composite values for 248 source pairs. All selected composite values are zero for the other 140 pairs. The workbook's zero is not zero affinity and does not establish noninteraction. The source IPI assertions remain intact; unresolved measurement/identity evidence is distinguished from negative biological evidence. Every row's original supporting entity, including isoform identifiers, is retained.

The table preserves COMP_neglogKd, its source method, independent FP/DAPF/CALIP/SAPF fields, peptide sequences, modifications and worksheet row numbers. Values are not averaged into an invented affinity, and no missing or zero value is replaced with a fabricated number. Composite values quoted in review reasons are source values rather than newly measured constants. The phage/peptide and isolated-domain assays do not establish native full-length binding, cellular colocalization, physiological relevance, or equivalent behavior of all DLG4 splice products.

Identity and assay cases that affect interpretation

  • AXIN1 has three selected internal-peptide measurements, all with zero composites. Its -INTERNAL- placeholder is not an amino-acid sequence; selection instead uses the explicit capped peptide core.
  • PDLIM4-1 and PDLIM4-2 remain separate partner identities. The alternative natural-tail candidates are not transferred between products. Their selected composites remain zero.
  • WHRN's unmatched internal candidates are excluded; its matching terminal-tail measurements remain zero.
  • Unmatched HPV33/HPV35 phosphopeptide candidates are excluded. In particular, the nonzero unmatched HPV35 candidate is not used as identity support; other sequence-supported measurements justify retaining the limited interaction.
  • RPS6KA1 has several modified and unmodified reagents. Its unmodified PDZ1 composite is 3.67923818; the retained interaction is not based only on phosphorylation-mimicking or phosphorylated ligands.
  • APBA1 has zero selected PDZ-tail composites but a separate positive BioPlex co-complex record. This does not make the PDZ experiment positive or prove a direct binary interface.
  • DLGAP4 has zero selected PDZ-tail composites, while the neuronal interaction map records recognition by the DLG4 GK fragment (546–724). A different domain can support scaffold association without contradicting the PDZ measurements.

Functional assessment

The molecular function of the full protein is not determined by the physical form of an assay reagent. The positive peptide/domain interfaces are retained as evidence without a blanket conversion to peptide-binding function. More informative partner-class refinements are made where independent biology supports them: glutamate receptors, potassium transporters, Preso, BCR, ACTN2, ERBB4 and DLGAP4. Other positive fragment interfaces remain non-core binding observations; zero-only cases without independent positive evidence remain uncertain.

The integrated DLG4 core is synaptic receptor-adaptor activity. Receptor recognition, phosphorylation-sensitive SH3-GK recognition and structural organization are cooperating parts of that scaffold, not automatically separate core functions. See the gene source guide for the independent originals and construct limits.

Reproduction

reproduce.py parses the original workbook and the exact review partner identities using identity-sequences.fasta and identity-provenance.tsv. It regenerates measurements.tsv, source-row-crosswalk.tsv and run-summary.json. --check compares generated bytes with those files without changing them. It fails if the workbook or sequence digests differ. The sequence provenance records public UniProt URLs; the frozen FASTA permits replay without assuming that a future official release has identical sequences.

Source Guide

(DLG4-source-guide.md)

DLG4 evidence and source guide

DLG4 (human P78352; HGNC:2903) has cooperating synaptic receptor-adaptor and structural postsynaptic-density roles. PDZ receptor recognition, SH3–GK recruitment and postsynaptic structural support are cooperating mechanisms. Binding a catalytic partner does not give PSD-95 that partner's activity. The official products are P78352-1 (724 residues), P78352-2 (767) and P78352-3 (721); historical constructs and domain fragments are not assumed to test all three products.

Reproducible interaction measurements

The fragmentomics results and executable analysis expose the original measurement values, exact source partner identities, peptide modifications and sequence-selection rules. The reproduction instructions use the published PMID:36115835 workbook and the saved official sequence inputs.

The workbook has 1,344 DLG4 measurements. Accession matching yields 1,197 candidate crosswalk records: 1,179 natural-sequence matches and 18 unmatched natural-sequence candidates. Three explicit AXIN1 internal peptides are additionally sequence-supported, giving 1,182 selected records. Of 388 source pairs, 248 have a nonzero selected composite and 140 have only zero selected composites. Zero is neither zero affinity nor proof of noninteraction. Unmatched candidates, including particular viral phosphopeptides, are not silently used as identity support.

Most positive isolated-domain interfaces remain non-core binding observations because their physiological role is not resolved. The exact project curation instruction supports retaining positive generic binding when an informative narrower function is not justified. Peptide reagents do not by themselves establish a physiological peptide-binding function. Supported specificity uses MODIFY, with the imported term and supporting entities retained.

Repeated partners were compared across sources. DLGAP1 scaffold recognition and its targeted phosphoprotein assay describe compatible aspects; SPAR's GAP class and phosphorylation-dependent recognition are likewise compatible. ERBB4 has independent receptor-tyrosine-kinase binding evidence despite the expression of concern on one later paper. APBA1 has independent BioPlex co-complex evidence, while its isolated PDZ-tail composites remain zero. DLGAP4 has independent GK-fragment recognition at residues 546–724; that does not convert its zero PDZ-tail measurements into positive results. Source-specific uncertainty is retained where no independent positive evidence resolves a zero-only fragment assertion.

The crystal is SAP97/phospho-LGN; it is not a PSD-95 crystal. Domain assays are not tests of every natural full-length product.

There is no blanket exclusion of epithelial function.

Additional selected originals support KIF1Balpha tail binding (12097473), receptor-associated complexes (17360663, 19243221, 22593058), BCR/ABR recognition (20962234), MTMR2 lipid-phosphatase recognition (20410104), MDM2 association (23260144), ADAM22 tail dependence (27066583), P2Y1 and D1 receptor contexts (20847060, 23041629), and presynaptic/juxtaparanodal pools (8922396, 19109503). Each reference assessment records its actual scope; no abstract-only entry is silently relabeled as a full-text cache. The DGK-iota paper (21119615) was accessed as primary indexed excerpts and supports lipid-kinase binding, not protein-kinase-specific recognition.

Publication concern

PMID:38114668(https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-023-02757-y) is an expression of concern for PMID:16767099(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16767099/). It identifies immunoblot-image concerns and unavailable original gels. The affected reference is DISPUTED, not retracted or marked invalid. Independent ERBB4 association evidence is assessed on its own merits.

Curated pathways and propagation

The two cached GO-CAM models already place DLG4 in adaptor roles: 62900b6400001630 uses synaptic receptor adaptor activity in the intracellular postsynaptic density with rat orthology support, and 67b1629100002554 uses macromolecule adaptor activity in the LGI1–ADAM22 context with mouse support. They do not make DLG4 a receptor, channel or enzyme.

The exact human Reactome paths distinguish target location from the activity of an entire complex. Public entity records are accessible through the Content Service:

Event Target-resolved path and interpretation
AMPA trafficking R-HSA-416320 202135 is P78352 at plasma membrane; 416847 is the endocytic-vesicle membrane pool.
Calcium influx R-HSA-432164 Catalyst/complex traversal reaches P78352 entity 202135; PSD-95 is not the channel pore.
Kainate binding R-HSA-451283, activation R-HSA-451311 Receptor complex components reach 202135; target complex membership is distinguished from receptor chemistry.
CIT-3 R-HSA-5671993, RAS exchange R-HSA-5672965 Input/output or catalyst-complex paths reach 202135. No kinase or exchange-factor activity is transferred to PSD-95.
LGI1 R-HSA-5682794 ADAM22/PSD-95/stargazin complex 5682831 contains the P78352 membrane entity.
ABP1/SHANK R-HSA-6797554 DLG2/3/4 set 6794325 includes P78352 cytosolic entity 6794267.
PSD-95/NMDA R-HSA-8849878, SALM/PSD-95 R-HSA-8849891, SALM1/NMDA R-HSA-8849906 Direct or complex paths reach 202135, through the PSD-95-family set 376003 or complex 8849869 where applicable.

Thirteen PAINT assertions were traced to literal IBD nodes on the human target's ancestral path, including PTN000563569, PTN001136892, PTN004609043, PTN002750666 and PTN008381197. A DLG1/SCRIB source can support an ancestral function; it is not automatically a paralog error. A short donor list and target self-evidence are not reasons to reject inheritance. Donor function, target biology and term scope are evaluated separately. Six ARBA conditions were matched to actual target CATH FunFam/InterPro assignments rather than inferred from a rule name.

Remaining boundaries

The specific endoplasmic-reticulum, synaptic-vesicle, cortical-cytoskeleton, mossy-fiber-rosette, dendritic-arborization and epithelial-polarity assertions remain uncertain where the available target-resolved evidence does not settle them. These are source/term-specific limits, not denials of established synaptic biology. No NEW annotation is proposed. The follow-up explicitly represents the complementary structural molecular role alongside receptor-adaptor activity.

Follow-up: quantitative thresholds and structural contribution

The fragmentomics Methods distinguish DAPF (double affinity-purified PDZ protein with fluorescence readout) normalized binding-intensity threshold 0.05 from LYSC/SAPF threshold 0.1. Effective Kd limits vary with peptide concentrations (30–790 µM, mean 320 µM); the smallest nonzero workbook composite is not a universal biological cutoff. The composite chooses a holdup method and does not replace independent fluorescence polarization. Of 729 zero composites across 1344 measurements, 380 have negative raw DAPF intensities. Four zero composites have positive FP measurements elsewhere in the grid, but none belongs to the selected measurements of the 138 uncertain source rows. All 414 selected measurements for those 138 rows use DAPF and remain below 0.05. Negative intensity is an assay estimate relative to a control; it is not negative affinity or a declaration of nonbinding. See PMID:36115835(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9482650/), Methods “Estimation of binding intensities”/holdup affinity calculations and Discussion on below-quantification pairs. The unchanged public workbook artifact exposes the values and exact sequence joins.

The structural core is grounded in PMID:21525273(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21525273/), Materials and Methods (rat hippocampal cultures, PSD95-EYFP constructs, immunogold/electron tomography), Results on PSD95-containing vertical filaments and their loss after RNAi, and Discussion on structural maintenance. These are E20 rat neurons; only a subset of filaments is immunolabeled, and receptor-type classifications are morphological/putative. The source does not imply universal loss of NMDA-receptor clusters. It supports physical structural participation, not simply a gene-knockdown phenotype. Current GO:0098919 has a part_of edge to GO:0099562. The latter's current definition contains a presynaptic/postsynaptic wording discrepancy; the proposal uses its postsynaptic label, linked structural activity and actual source, not a presynaptic claim.

The PMID:26609151 original, Results “Enhanced activity-dependent degradation” and Figure 7A–C, reports: “Our results confirmed that PSD-95 is degraded in an activity-dependent manner”. This eleven-word original-only anchor is distinct from the abstract-only normal cache. The actual experiment uses mouse hippocampal neurons, 50 mM KCl for 15 min and proteasome inhibition; the significant additional genotype effect is on PSD-93. Accordingly the two potassium-response judgments retain the real abundance observation but do not infer a performed response step from being degraded. No original-only quotation is placed in cache-validated YAML.

id: P78352
gene_symbol: DLG4
product_type: PROTEIN
status: DRAFT
taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:9606
  label: Homo sapiens
description: DLG4 encodes PSD-95, a membrane-associated guanylate kinase family scaffold concentrated
  in the intracellular postsynaptic density of excitatory synapses. Its PDZ domains recognize receptor
  and accessory-protein tails, while its SH3–GK region recruits signaling and scaffold partners, including
  phosphorylation-dependent ligands. Together these contacts organize neurotransmitter receptors and downstream
  signaling machinery, support receptor targeting and maintain postsynaptic architecture. The GK-like
  domain functions in recognition rather than guanylate kinase catalysis. PSD-95 also occupies trafficking,
  presynaptic and non-neuronal junctional pools in particular contexts. Alternative N termini provide
  distinct targeting mechanisms, including the palmitoylation-associated alpha and L27-containing beta
  forms.
alternative_products:
- name: 1 (PSD95-alpha)
  id: P78352-1
  description: The 724-residue PSD95-alpha product has the canonical N-terminal palmitoylation motif and
    the shared three PDZ domains and SH3–GK region.
- name: 2 (PSD95-beta)
  id: P78352-2
  sequence_note: VSP_014929
  description: The 767-residue PSD95-beta product replaces alpha residues 1–10 with a distinct 53-residue
    N terminus. This changes the alpha palmitoylation motif and supplies the beta-specific targeting region.
- name: '3'
  id: P78352-3
  sequence_note: VSP_047247
  description: This 721-residue product lacks canonical residues 51–53 and retains the shared PDZ and
    SH3–GK regions. Its distinct trafficking behavior has not been established by the product-specific
    experiments assessed here.

      These PSD-95 assays are distinct from the SAP97 structural experiments. Phosphoprotein binding captures
      the measured recognition mechanism; it does not infer kinase activity, all-product equivalence or
      full-length native stoichiometry.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0051219
      label: phosphoprotein binding

  review:

    action: MODIFY
    reason: The original includes PSD-95/MDM2 coimmunoprecipitation and recombinant GST/His interaction
      assays in the source-specific mouse/heterologous context. MDM2 is the E3 enzyme; PSD-95 is its binding

  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P60893
  review:
    summary: Retain motif-dependent association with the orphan receptor GPR85.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The actual original tests a human GPR85 C-terminal sequence against PSD-95 in mouse-brain
      and COS-cell extracts. Deleting YCVI abolishes the association and PDZ1 is implicated. This is controlled
      receptor-tail recognition, but the receptor remains orphan and the assay does not resolve a DLG4-dependent
      ligand-triggered signaling function. Keep the positive association without inferring a specific
      signaling subclass or transferring the reported GPR85-variant phenotypes.

    label: protein binding

  original_reference_id: PMID:27066583
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9P0K1
  review:
    summary: Retain ADAM22 association in the neuronal scaffold.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: 'The source tests human ADAM22 variants: wild type and C401Y retain PSD-95 binding, whereas
      the frameshift removing the terminal PDZ-binding motif does not. ADAM22 is a noncatalytic metalloprotease-like
      receptor. This supports scaffold association without enzyme-binding inference from its family name
      or a claim that PSD-95 has ADAM22 ligand activity.'

  supporting_entities:

  review:
    summary: Retain the source-specific PDZ3–tail interaction.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The literal source records a DLG4 PDZ3 construct (residues 313–388) against a nine-residue
      partner tail in the phosphomimetic phage-display study. The library compares native and S/T-to-Glu
      variants; such a display hit is not full-length physiological validation or direct evidence of phosphorylation
      in cells. Preserve the positive interface without assigning a separate peptide function or automatically
      transferring the full partner class to DLG4.

      validation is claimed for the display experiment itself.

  review:
    summary: The PPP1R3G source-pair assertion remains unresolved at the recovered measurement level.
    action: UNDECIDED
    reason: The published SD1 workbook resolves 3 sequence-supported measurement(s) for B7ZBB8 (PPP1R3G;
      taxon 9606); maximum source COMP values by tested domain are PDZ1=0, PDZ2=0, PDZ3=0. The selected
      DAPF records are below the normalized binding-intensity quantification threshold of 0.05 (range
      -0.012306 to 0.021925), and none has a positive matched fluorescence-polarization measurement. Their
      zero composite is a censored assay result, not zero affinity. Negative binding intensities represent
      no measurable depletion relative to the control and experimental noise, not negative affinity. The
      original study explicitly cautions that below-threshold pairs are not demonstrated noninteractions.
      The imported positive IPI assertion is preserved, but binding for these specific fragments remains
      unquantified; neither a credible positive interface nor absence of binding is established. Retain
      source-specific uncertainty without inferring a native full-length role.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:36115835
      supporting_text: pairs that fell below holdup quantification threshold should not be considered
        as “non-interactions”.

      does not establish the physiological role of the full-length pair. Retain positive binding without
      naming a free-peptide biological function or importing an enzymatic/receptor subclass solely from
      the partner identity.

  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P10499
  review:
    summary: Specify binding to the identified potassium-channel partner.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The curated original-source records explicitly pair human DLG4 PDZ-region constructs with
      the indicated rat Kv1 channel, using two-hybrid and far-western assays and relevant tail/domain
      controls. The original abstract supports channel clustering, but the full paper was not independently
      recovered. Transmembrane-transporter binding describes the established interface class without making
      DLG4 a channel, asserting identical affinity for every Kv1 subtype or erasing the cross-species
      assay.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0044325
      label: transmembrane transporter binding

  review:
    summary: Resolve broad cytoplasmic localization into supported intracellular pools.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The imported orthology/rule assignment is biologically sound. PSD-95 occupies a soluble cytosolic
      pool as well as the intracellular postsynaptic density and trafficking-associated endocytic-vesicle
      membrane. Rat/heterologous localization and the explicit P78352 Reactome entities independently
      support these locations. These replacements describe verified pools, not exclusive localization
      or equivalent trafficking of all three natural products.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0005829
      label: cytosol
    - id: GO:0099092
      label: postsynaptic density, intracellular component
    - id: GO:0030666
      label: endocytic vesicle membrane

        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER

          rows are retained in the source projection. This records donor/source tracing, not a claim that

- term:
    id: GO:0005886
    label: plasma membrane
  evidence_type: EXP
  original_reference_id: PMID:12151521
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: DLG4 associates with the plasma membrane in several cellular contexts.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: Plasma-membrane association is valid and deliberately retains the range of neuronal and nonneuronal
      contexts. The beta/alpha localization study, ortholog evidence and mouse embryonic epithelial imaging
      support multiple membrane pools, rather than an exclusive postsynaptic compartment. The HPA summary
      is currently uncertain and is not treated as the sole localization proof. Product-specific targeting
      mechanisms and the source-specific assay limitations remain separate.
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:12151521
    - PMID:21920314
    - PMID:16520334

  review:
    summary: DLG4 is a plasma-membrane-associated component of the modeled signaling assembly.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The event-specific typed Reactome input/output or catalyst-complex path reaches the actual

- term:
    id: GO:0005912
    label: adherens junction
  evidence_type: NAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:23397623
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: Generalize the epithelial location to the independently supported cell junction.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The examined PMID:23397623 adherens-junction mechanism explicitly concerns mammalian DLG1
      and Scribble; it does not establish the cadherin-catenin-defined junction for DLG4. Independent
      original PMID:21920314 directly images mouse Dlg4 at epithelial cell junctions and broadly along
      the plasma membrane, supporting the less specific cell-junction assignment. This preserves positive
      epithelial localization without transferring DLG1-specific adherens-junction machinery.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0030054
      label: cell junction
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:21920314
- term:
    id: GO:0007165
    label: signal transduction
  evidence_type: TAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:10364559
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: Specify the NMDA-receptor signaling context.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The source abstract directly reports that PSD-95 depletion uncouples NMDAR activation from
      nitric-oxide signaling while leaving receptor currents and calcium entry intact. Together with the
      established receptor-adaptor mechanism, this supports the existing NMDA-selective glutamate-receptor
      signaling term rather than undifferentiated signal transduction. The abstract does not establish
      the species or every construct; those are not invented.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0098989
      label: NMDA selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway
- term:
    id: GO:0007204
    label: positive regulation of cytosolic calcium ion concentration
  evidence_type: ISS
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000024
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P31016
  review:
    summary: PSD-95 restrains the tested 5-HT2A receptor calcium response.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The literal donor annotation assigns positive regulation, but the indexed primary Results
      and Figure 3 of PMID:20531396 show that disrupting the 5-HT2A PDZ interface or reducing PSD-95 unmasks
      a receptor-dependent calcium response. A terminal-mutant peptide, scrambled RNA and a 5-HT2A antagonist
      provide controls. This supports negative regulation in that specific neuronal receptor assay, not
      a global assertion that DLG4 decreases calcium in every context. The original positive source term
      and donor identity remain unchanged. The indexed primary excerpts include calcium-imaging methods,
      but do not establish the species of the neuronal culture.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0051481
      label: negative regulation of cytosolic calcium ion concentration
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: TERM_SCOPING_PROBLEM
      source_entities:
      - source_id: UniProtKB:P31016
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: The current donor record contains the exact transferred term; literal evidence/reference
          rows are retained in the source projection. This records donor/source tracing, not a claim that
          every cited original was recovered. The primary receptor-specific experiment supports an inhibitory
          effect; the concern is the positive sign of this annotation, not the quality of the paper or
          donor ancestry.
      failure_modes:
      - REGULATORY_SIGN_INVERSION
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:20531396
      supporting_text: 'it revealed functional 5-HT(2A) receptor-operated Ca(2+) responses in neurons,

        an effect mimicked by knockdown of PSD-95.'
- term:
    id: GO:0007268
    label: chemical synaptic transmission
  evidence_type: IBA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000033
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - FB:FBgn0001624
  - MGI:MGI:1344351
  - PANTHER:PTN000563569
  review:
    summary: DLG4 contributes to chemical synaptic transmission as a receptor scaffold.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The conserved adaptor organizes neurotransmitter receptors and associated signaling proteins.
      The PAINT assertion is placed on the actual ancestral lineage, the InterPro mapping is literal,
      and the mouse PSD-95 mutant study demonstrates altered synaptic plasticity. This is scaffold participation
      in transmission, not neurotransmitter release or channel activity attributed to DLG4.
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:9853749
    - PMID:17046693
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: NO_FAILURE_CORE
      source_entities:
      - source_id: PANTHER:PTN000563569
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: 'Literal IBD at the Bilateria node on the actual human target path. Descendant evidence:
          MGI:MGI:1344351|FB:FBgn0001624. The target appearing among descendant sources is not circular
          evidence.'

    label: learning
  evidence_type: TAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:9853749
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: Retain the learning phenotype as a non-core organismal process.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The source explicitly reports impaired spatial learning in PSD-95 mutant mice alongside shifted

      the curated organismal association, not a separate learning-specific molecular activity or a new
      human assay.

  evidence_type: ISS
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000024
  qualifier: colocalizes_with
  supporting_entities:

  review:
    summary: PSD-95 is a scaffold component of voltage-gated potassium-channel complexes.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The literal rat donor is grounded in PMID:20089912. Rat-brain co-immunoprecipitation detects
      PSD-95 with Kv1.2, ADAM22 and other scaffold components, while heterologous clustering supports
      assembly. This denotes complex membership; coexpression did not change the measured Kv1.2 electrophysiological
      properties and does not make PSD-95 a channel subunit that forms the pore.

    label: protein kinase binding
  evidence_type: IBA

  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - PANTHER:PTN001136892
  - RGD:2505
  - RGD:68424
  - RGD:708527
  review:
    summary: Retain inherited protein-kinase binding separately from the DGKI interaction.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The source is a genuine PAINT IBD on ancestral PTN001136892 with experimental rat-family grounding,
      including the Dlg4 lineage. Its protein-kinase claim is distinct from the lipid-kinase assay in
      PMID:21119615. Preserve the supported partner class without inferring catalysis or treating a source
      containing the target as circular.

      root_cause: NO_FAILURE_NON_CORE
      source_entities:
      - source_id: PANTHER:PTN001136892
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: 'Literal IBD at the Metazoa-Choanoflagellida node on the actual human target path. Descendant
          evidence: RGD:708527|RGD:68424|RGD:2505. The target appearing among descendant sources is not
          circular evidence.'
- term:
    id: GO:0019903
    label: protein phosphatase binding
  evidence_type: ISS
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000024
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P31016
  review:
    summary: Generalize the experimentally grounded partner class to phosphatase binding.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The literal rat donor IPI evidence points to PMID:20410104. That original tests PSD-95 association
      with MTMR2, a phosphoinositide phosphatase, using motif controls and cellular/brain complexes. It
      does not establish protein-phosphatase substrate specificity for that partner. GO:0019902 retains
      the demonstrated phosphatase interaction without the erroneous protein-phosphatase restriction.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0019902
      label: phosphatase binding
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:20410104
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: TERM_SCOPING_PROBLEM
      source_entities:
      - source_id: UniProtKB:P31016
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: The current donor record contains the exact transferred term; literal evidence/reference
          rows are retained in the source projection. This records donor/source tracing, not a claim that
          every cited original was recovered.The original partner MTMR2 is a lipid phosphatase; the protein-phosphatase
          restriction is not retained.
      failure_modes:
      - GRANULARITY_MISMATCH

- term:
    id: GO:0035418
    label: protein localization to synapse
  evidence_type: IBA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000033
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - MGI:MGI:107231
  - MGI:MGI:1277959
  - MGI:MGI:1344351
  - PANTHER:PTN000563569
  - RGD:2505
  - RGD:68424
  - UniProtKB:P78352
  review:
    summary: DLG4 helps position multiple proteins at synapses.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The source original tests assembly and targeting of PSD-95/GKAP/Shank complexes, and independent
      work shows receptor targeting. Because the cargo includes receptors and other scaffold/signaling
      proteins, protein localization to synapse remains a useful inclusive process rather than being collapsed
      to receptors alone. The PAINT target self-source is legitimate experimental grounding; the ARBA
      conditions also match the official protein.
    additional_reference_ids:

- term:
    id: GO:0035418
    label: protein localization to synapse
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:15496675
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: DLG4 helps position multiple proteins at synapses.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The source original tests assembly and targeting of PSD-95/GKAP/Shank complexes, and independent
      work shows receptor targeting. Because the cargo includes receptors and other scaffold/signaling
      proteins, protein localization to synapse remains a useful inclusive process rather than being collapsed
      to receptors alone. The PAINT target self-source is legitimate experimental grounding; the ARBA
      conditions also match the official protein.

- term:
    id: GO:0035865
    label: cellular response to potassium ion
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000107
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q62108
  - ensembl:ENSMUSP00000156345
  review:
    summary: The cited potassium-stimulation result measures regulation of PSD-95 abundance.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: Original PMID:26609151 shows PSD-95 loss after high-KCl stimulation, blocked by proteasome
      inhibition. The significant additional MAP1A-dependent effect concerns PSD-93, not PSD-95. These
      particular experiments establish regulated PSD-95 degradation without resolving a contribution by
      DLG4 to the cellular potassium-response process. The process assignment therefore exceeds the specific
      assay, while the measured change remains valid. This is not a universal rejection of response-term
      inference from regulated abundance.
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:26609151
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: TERM_SCOPING_PROBLEM
      source_entities:
      - source_id: UniProtKB:Q62108
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: The current donor record contains the exact transferred term; literal evidence/reference
          rows are retained in the source projection. This records donor/source tracing, not a claim that
          every cited original was recovered. The original regulated-degradation observation is valid;
          its process interpretation is the scoped concern.
      failure_modes:
      - ROLE_CONFLATION
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:26609151

- term:
    id: GO:0045197
    label: establishment or maintenance of epithelial cell apical/basal polarity
  evidence_type: NAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:23397623
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: A DLG4-specific epithelial apicobasal-polarity role remains unresolved.
    action: UNDECIDED
    reason: The examined full PMID:23397623 review attributes the operative mammalian polarity and adherens-junction
      mechanisms to DLG1 and Scribble. Separately, mouse Dlg4 is positively localized at epithelial cell
      junctions and broadly along plasma membrane, but localization alone does not demonstrate that it
      establishes apicobasal polarity. This is uncertainty about the specific process, not a blanket denial
      of epithelial DLG4 function.
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:21920314

- id: PMID:10364559
  title: Specific coupling of NMDA receptor activation to nitric oxide neurotoxicity by PSD-95 protein.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The abstract links PSD-95 to coupling NMDA receptor activation with nitric-oxide-associated
      neurotoxicity. It supports the receptor signaling context; original Methods were not recovered.
- id: PMID:10433268
  title: Shank, a novel family of postsynaptic density proteins that binds to the NMDA receptor/PSD-95/GKAP
    complex and cortactin.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The abstract describes the Shank–GKAP–PSD-95 organization. Exact pair-specific panels
      were not recovered; curated partner records and independent channel/scaffold evidence are distinguished
      from a personally verified original assay.
- id: PMID:10725395
  title: The neuregulin receptor ErbB-4 interacts with PDZ-containing proteins at neuronal synapses.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Original selected Results and Methods directly support ERBB4 association with PSD-95,
      including PDZ dependence, heterologous tests and brain material. Those assays remain independent
      of the later disputed schizophrenia study. The initial normal abstract is retained in provenance;
      the published cache reuses the unchanged genuine full-text DLG3 cache after explicit identity and
      byte reconciliation.
- id: PMID:10859302
  title: GAKIN, a novel kinesin-like protein associates with the human homologue of the Drosophila discs
    large tumor suppressor in T lymphocytes.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly reports GAKIN binding to the PSD-95 GK region despite
      its emphasis on hDlg. Full original construct details remain unavailable.
- id: PMID:11937501
  title: Selectivity and promiscuity of the first and second PDZ domains of PSD-95 and synapse-associated
    protein 102.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract reports fluorescence-polarization and ELISA measurements of PSD-95/SAP102
      PDZ recognition. Curated partner records retain exact receptor/channel and isoform identities; not
      every original target panel was independently recovered.
- id: PMID:12097473
  title: Association of the kinesin superfamily motor protein KIF1Balpha with postsynaptic density-95
    (PSD-95), synapse-associated protein-97, and synaptic scaffolding molecule PSD-95/discs large/zona
    occludens-1 proteins.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected original experiments show rat KIF1Balpha tail-dependent association using mutation
      and binding controls. The imported human partner maps to O60333-3; human identity mapping and rat
      assay provenance remain distinct.
- id: PMID:12151521
  title: Postsynaptic targeting of alternative postsynaptic density-95 isoforms by distinct mechanisms.
  findings:
  - statement: Alpha and beta PSD-95 constructs use distinct postsynaptic targeting mechanisms.
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Separately recovered primary indexed Methods/Results establish distinct alpha/beta targeting,
      including a human beta N-terminal cDNA insert, rat neuronal cultures and COS-cell assays. The whole
      alpha-backbone species is unresolved; the normal cache remains abstract-only.
- id: PMID:12713445
  title: Selective interaction of megalin with postsynaptic density-95 (PSD-95)-like membrane-associated
    guanylate kinase (MAGUK) proteins.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The abstract supports megalin/LRP2 association with PSD-95-like proteins in trafficking
      contexts. It does not establish ligand-initiated signaling by the particular DLG4 interface.
- id: PMID:15496675
  title: A functional role of postsynaptic density-95-guanylate kinase-associated protein complex in regulating
    Shank assembly and stability to synapses.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected original neuronal and heterologous experiments support cooperation of PSD-95,
      GKAP and Shank in synaptic assembly. Transport of a preassembled complex is an interpretation rather
      than a directly measured transport step.
- id: PMID:16767099
  title: Altered neuregulin 1-erbB4 signaling contributes to NMDA receptor hypofunction in schizophrenia.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: DISPUTED
    review_notes: The primary association report is subject to the verified expression of concern PMID:38114668
      concerning several immunoblot figures and unavailable original gels. This is not a retraction. Independent
      ERBB4 association experiments remain separate evidence.
- id: PMID:17360663
  title: HIV-tat induces formation of an LRP-PSD-95- NMDAR-nNOS complex that promotes apoptosis in neurons
    and astrocytes.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED

- id: PMID:36115835
  title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
  findings:
  - statement: Isolated DLG4 PDZ domains recognize defined peptide ligands with source-specific measurement
      and identity limits.
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Original workbook measurements were independently parsed against exact partner sequences.
      The public artifact preserves all 1,344 DLG4 domain measurements and the 1,182 selected sequence-supported
      records. The 138 zero-only undecided source rows have DAPF normalized binding intensities below 0.05
      and no selected positive fluorescence-polarization result. These are below-quantification observations;
      the original Discussion explicitly rejects interpreting them as demonstrated noninteractions. Holdup
      sensitivity depends on method and peptide concentration.

- id: file:human/DLG4/DLG4-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md
  title: 'DLG4 fragmentomics: source values and interpretation'
  findings:
  - statement: Sequence-supported crosswalks distinguish candidate partner matches from selected measurements
      and preserve all original assay values.
core_functions:
- description: PSD-95 bridges synaptic receptors and downstream signaling/scaffold proteins through PDZ-mediated
    receptor recognition and SH3–GK partner recruitment. These contacts organize receptor targeting and
    signaling at excitatory postsynaptic sites.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0030160
    label: synaptic receptor adaptor activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0099645
    label: neurotransmitter receptor localization to postsynaptic specialization membrane
  locations:
  - id: GO:0099092
    label: postsynaptic density, intracellular component
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:22117215
    supporting_text: The bindings of PSD-95 SH3-GK to DLGAP1 and SPAR are also phosphorylation-dependent
  - reference_id: PMID:17046693
    supporting_text: PSD-95 and PSD-93 independently mediate AMPA-R targeting at mature synapses.
- description: PSD-95 provides structural elements of the intracellular postsynaptic density that maintain
    its protein organization and stabilize receptor-associated scaffold assemblies. This architectural
    role cooperates with its receptor-adaptor activity.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0098919
    label: structural constituent of postsynaptic density
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0099562
    label: maintenance of postsynaptic density structure
  locations:
  - id: GO:0099092
    label: postsynaptic density, intracellular component
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:21525273
suggested_questions:
- question: Which zero-composite or identity-unresolved PDZ fragment pairs can be confirmed with the exact
    native partner sequence and an independently controlled full-length assay?
- question: What trafficking and interaction properties distinguish the natural 721-residue product from
    PSD95-alpha and PSD95-beta?
- question: What target-resolved evidence supports the specific endoplasmic-reticulum, synaptic-vesicle,
    mossy-fiber-rosette and epithelial-polarity assertions that remain uncertain?
